facts.statement: Colombian paleontologist María Páramo defined the new genus and species Yaguarasaurus columbianus based on an articulated skull, some vertebrae, and ribs.
facts.quote: The remains discovered (an articulated skull, some vertebrae and ribs) were defined as a new genus and species of mosasaurid, Yaguarasaurus columbianus, by the Colombian paleontologist María Páramo

facts.statement: Yaguarasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous (Turonian) period in Colombia, South America.
facts.quote: Yaguarasaurus is an extinct genus of mosasauroid from the Late Cretaceous (Turonian) period of Colombia, South America

facts.statement: An additional skull measuring 87 cm long implies that the animal could have been larger than the initial estimates.
facts.quote: an additional skull that measures 87 cm long implies a larger size

facts.statement: Remains were found in an Upper Turonian limestone bed of the La Frontera Formation near Yaguará, Huila, at a site called Cueva Rica.
facts.quote: The remains were found in a limestone bed (Upper Turonian) of the La Frontera Formation, member of the Villeta Group, near Yaguará, Huila, in a site called Cueva Rica

facts.statement: The name Yaguarasaurus means "Yaguará lizard of Colombia".
facts.quote: Its name means "Yaguará lizard of Colombia"

facts.statement: A 2023 hypothesis by Rivera-Sylva et al. classifies Yaguarasaurus as a basal member of the Plioplatecarpinae.
facts.quote: Topology B follows Rivera-Sylva et al. (2023) and depicts a new hypothesis holding Yaguarasaurus as a basal member of the Plioplatecarpinae

facts.statement: The species is classified within the subfamily Yaguarasaurinae.
Palci et al. (2013) created the subfamily Yaguarasaurinae, which is the sister group to Tethysaurinae.
facts.quote: Palci et al. (2013) describen a un nuevo russellosaurino, Romeosaurus, y crean la subfamilia Yaguarasaurinae, que es el grupo hermano de Tethysaurinae

facts.statement: An analysis by Makádi et al. (2012) grouped Yaguarasaurus with other primitive mosasaurs into the subfamily Tethysaurinae.
facts.quote: el siguiente cladograma sigue el análisis de Makádi et al. de 2012

facts.statement: Yaguarasaurus lived approximately 90 million years ago during the Upper Cretaceous (Turonian) in Colombia.
facts.quote: Yaguarasaurus es un género extinto de mosasaurio procedente del período Cretácico Superior (Turoniense, hace aproximadamente 90 millones de años) de Colombia, Suramérica

facts.statement: Early fossils suggested a total length of approximately 5 meters based on a cranial length of 47 centimeters.
facts.quote: Los primeros fósiles del animal sugirieron que podía medir aproximadamente 5 metros de longitud, basándose en la longitud craneal de 47 centímetros

facts.statement: Additional remains suggest even larger sizes, with one skull reaching a cranial length of 87 centimeters.
facts.quote: Restos adicionales sugieren tamaños aun mayores, ya que un cráneo llegaba a una longitud craneal de 87 centímetros

facts.statement: The Yaguarasaurus discovered in Yaguará is now among the most complete materials known in South America.
facts.quote: Este mosasaurio descubierto en Yaguará, está ahora entre los más completos materiales conocidos en América del Sur

facts.statement: After the discovery of Pannoniasaurus, it became clear that Yaguarasaurus and other "russellosaurines" formed a clade of primitive amphibious mosasaurs related to the aigialosaurs.
facts.quote: Tras el hallazgo del mosasauroideo primitivo de Hungría Pannoniasaurus por Makádi et al. 2012 quedó claro que Yaguarasaurus y los demás "russellosaurinos" formaban un clado de mosasaurios primitivos anfibios emparentados con los aigialosáuridos

facts.statement: The time range for Yaguarasaurus is the Turonian to Coniacian, from 93.9 to 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Initial fossil remains suggested a cranial length of 47 cm and a total body length of 5 meters.
rejected.quote: The first fossils remains of this animal suggested a cranial length of 47 cm and a total length of 5 m
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'suggested a cranial length of 47 cm and'

rejected.statement: Under the 2023 hypothesis, the two species of Yaguarasaurus are considered paraphyletic relative to more derived plioplatecarpines.
rejected.quote: In the second scenario, the two species of Yaguarasaurus are paraphyletic with respect to more derived plioplatecarpines
